description: This mural, located beside the Bendale Library, celebrates reading and its ability to open the door to adventure and the discovery of new ideas, by depicting readers of all ages and backgrounds immersed in books and their imagination.

This mural depicts two abstract yarn bundles, signifying the importance of the yarn industry to the local community, while allowing for personal interpretation. The pedestrian tunnels are painted with colourful stripes to enliven the space.

name: A Bit of England Far From England

description: This mural depicts the natural and First Nations context of the area and promotes environmental preservation by incorporating the area's three distinct eco-systems and animals that historically thrived (but not longer live) in the area.

description: This mural incorporates a colourful ribbon protectively wrapping around the Women's Residence. The project was run by a women-led team and involved women from the Residence.

name: Raft of Medusa: Survivors
description: This mural reinterprets a 19th century painting of the same name by French artist Théodore Géricault to show the heart and soul of the Kensington Market community.

name: The Original People Leading to the Eighth Fire
description: This mural replaced a romantic colonial scene with imagery that reflects the Indigenous roots of the area as well as the present urban community and vision for a sustainable future.
16 murals on garage doors in the laneway behind homes on the south side of Dundas St West (facing Trinity Bellwoods Park) were painted with various colourful designs.

name: You've Changed
description: Located adjacent to the historic walls of CAMH, this mural's positive message "You've Changed" is a commentary on our evolving views on CAMH and mental health, and also references the revitalization of the neighbourhood more broadly.

This mural honours the local neighbourhood's social and support networks, particularly the large proportion of Ward 21 residents employed in the social and health care industries who take care of one another and infuse the city with love.
